extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, publishers, researchers, and others interested in using preprints and open peer review
extracted.subtask_short: journals integrating preprints into peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Practices and policy options for journals to use preprints to support, open, and accelerate peer review (e.g., editorial policies, platform partnerships, community review, reviewed preprints). Targeted at stakeholders designing or evaluating journal peer-review workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial policies allowing/encouraging preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial policies that allow or encourage deposition of manuscripts at preprint servers (i.e., journals explicitly permit or promote posting preprints).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include Springer Nature journals; such policies support rapid dissemination and make preprints an accepted communication format for research findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnering with independent review services (Review Commons)
rubrics_metrics.description: Partner with platforms like Review Commons which provide journals with high-quality referee reports to reduce re-review rounds and shorten the publishing process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using an external, high-quality referee report provider can reduce duplicate reviewing and re-review cycles and speed editorial decisions (see Review Commons and affiliate journals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual submission integration with preprint servers
rubrics_metrics.description: Partnerships that allow authors to submit preprints to both the journal submission system and the preprint server (streamlined or linked submission workflows).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Development and PLOS have workflows to allow simultaneous submission to journal and preprint server, lowering friction for authors to post preprints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal-hosted community review/discussion forums
rubrics_metrics.description: Posting manuscripts as preprints on the journal’s own discussion forums to enable public peer review in the form of invited referee comments, author comments, editor comments, and community comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This enables journal-coordinated reviews and open community reviews to run in parallel, supports transparent discussion, and can help integrate community feedback into the editorial process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public posting of reviews and author responses (open peer review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Making peer reviews and authors' responses publicly available so stakeholders can objectively understand the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Described as 'lifting the veil' — public reviews have training/educational value for early-career researchers, support transparency, and create a space for dialogue among authors, editors, reviewers, and the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer constructiveness and civility (tone)
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviews are public, reviewers are expected to be constructive and kind and to structure feedback to improve the science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open visibility 'forces reviewers to be constructive and kind'; journals adopting open review can expect improved tone and more actionable feedback as a consequence of public accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor attention to community comments and author responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors should monitor public/community comments and may request authors to respond; while invited reviewers are not required to consider public comments, editors can integrate those comments into editorial decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Community reviews hosted on journal discussion boards can be more easily integrated into the official review process than reviews on third-party platforms; editors play a gatekeeping role in whether and how public comments affect decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public accountability encouraging higher-quality submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The expectation that feedback will be public can potentially encourage authors to submit higher-quality work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open review may deter low-quality submissions because reviews are visible, but journals should balance this against the risk that negative public reviews could affect perceived credibility of authors or studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency enabling detection of data problems and research integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Open community scrutiny increases the likelihood of detecting data manipulation or other problems, thereby improving research quality and integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Having 'more eyes on the study' can improve the odds of finding issues; journals can leverage community engagement as a quality-control mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial models publishing reviewed preprints (no accept/reject)
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternative editorial model where the journal publishes every paper it reviews as a Reviewed Preprint that includes the manuscript and the journal’s peer reviews, with assessments of rigor and significance, rather than making accept/reject decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: eLife's model aims to produce public peer reviews that highlight science and evaluate rigor/significance, shifting away from traditional binary editorial outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collecting and analyzing review-process metadata for meta-research
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintaining open and quantifiable records of the review process (including demographic and career-stage data of participants) to enable meta-research on peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metadata analysis can reveal who engages with peer review and in what ways, providing ethnographic and evaluative insights to improve peer-review systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of institutional or governmental constraints on preprinting
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that authors employed by governmental agencies or other institutions may face additional approval steps or restrictions that deter posting preprints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals promoting preprints should be aware of and accommodate such constraints (e.g., by offering flexible timelines or guidance) to avoid excluding affected authors.
